caption: The drawing depicts a section of a staircase featuring four wooden balusters and a newel post. The objects are oriented vertically, with the largest, most detailed baluster—presumably the newel post—positioned prominently in the left foreground. It is thick, has a rounded form with a slight waist, and sits atop a square base. Three thinner, uniformly shaped balusters stand in a row to the right of the newel post; each is elongated and tapers somewhat towards the top, with a bulging, rounded shape near the base where they connect to the stair treads. All the balusters and the newel post have a polished, reddish-brown wood appearance. The objects are set against a plain background rendered in shades of pale beige and gray, with linear elements suggesting stairs and wall paneling without intricate details. The visible steps are colored in muted grayish tones, and the surrounding floor boards are lightly outlined. The composition is vertically oriented and enclosed within a rectangle centrally positioned on a cream-colored sheet. At the bottom, some faint handwritten text is present.
title: Newel Post
